customer_question: Our chipset vendor created a Subset DN that removes a feature our product no longer supports (Power Class 1 in one case, AoA/AoD in another). Does that Subset DN actually resolve the inter-layer consistency concern we'd previously raised, and can we still use our existing RF/RF PHY test report as evidence under it?
question_variants: Does removing Power Class 1 support via a vendor Subset DN clear our earlier consistency concern?
Will a Subset DN with AoA/AoD support deleted let us keep using our existing test report?
Can the vendor's feature-removal Subset DN be verified before we commit to using it?
Is a Subset DN safe to register against, or will it still fail Consistency Check?
actual_issue: The customer's products supported chipset features (Power Class 1 on one product, AoA/AoD on another) that were no longer applicable, creating a risk of inter-layer Consistency Check failure between the chipset's RF/RF PHY layer and the rest of the design. The chipset vendor responded by issuing Subset DNs with those features removed, but it was not yet confirmed whether registering against the Subset DN would actually resolve the consistency exposure or still allow reuse of the existing RF/RF PHY test report.
plain_english_explanation: Sometimes a chip supports more features than a finished product actually uses, and if those extra features don't line up correctly with the other certified parts, the registration can fail an automated consistency check. The chip vendor can issue a trimmed-down version of their certification (a 'Subset') that removes the unused feature. Before relying on that trimmed-down version, the consultant ran it through a test registration to make sure it would actually pass the consistency check and that the original test report could still be used as proof.
consultant_answer: The consultant created a temporary/dummy project in their own Qualification Workspace to register against each vendor Subset DN before the customer committed to it. For the Power Class 1 removal (Subset DN against QCA66988-based QDID, for HM26): confirmed no LL-RF PHY inter-layer inconsistency around Class 1, and that any other inter-layer items were the same Test Case Waiver (TCW) items already applicable to the related QDID -- meaning the existing RF/RF PHY test report can be used as evidence for the Controller (Controller Subsystem) registration under this Subset DN without issue. For the AoA/AoD removal (QCA6595-based QDID, for HM23): after the vendor confirmed completion, the consultant similarly created a temporary project and confirmed the consistency problem was resolved.
decision_logic: A vendor's feature-removal Subset DN should not be assumed to resolve a consistency concern just because the unsupported feature was deleted from its ICS; it must be verified by running a temporary registration project through the actual Consistency Check before committing, confirming both that no new inter-layer inconsistency is introduced and that any remaining flagged items are already-covered TCW items rather than new failures.
final_recommendation: Before relying on a vendor's feature-removal Subset DN, build a temporary project in the certification Workspace using that Subset DN and run Consistency Check to confirm there is no new inter-layer inconsistency and that the existing RF/RF PHY test report can still serve as registration evidence; only proceed with the real registration once this is confirmed.
risk_if_done_wrong: Registering directly against a vendor's feature-removal Subset DN without first verifying it in a temporary project risks an inter-layer Consistency Check failure surfacing only after the real registration is underway, and risks losing the ability to reuse the existing RF/RF PHY test report as evidence.
